(1) consent forms for genomic sequencing are not consistent in their terminology and (2) they often do not provide enough information for patients to make informed decisions about the return of unsolicited and secondary genomic results.
75% of the diagnostic genomic sequencing consent forms that we analyzed addressed unsolicited findings and secondary findings, and that 25% did not address either type of finding.

there is a need for a standard terminology for reporting UF and SF, as well as a need to improve the clarity of consent forms.
